gloss: kindness · parental love — and, in Buddhist texts, loving-kindness (maitrī)
formNote: The Shuowen: 慈，愛也。从心，茲聲 — “love; from heart, with 茲 as the sound.” 心 sits at the foot of the graph.
summary: Kindness, especially a parent’s for a child (父慈子孝). Buddhist translators gave 慈 the word maitrī, loving-kindness, first of the Four Immeasurables; and Maitreya, the Buddha to come, is also called 慈氏, “the Kind One”.
placement: On the left of the sphere's equator, above 有, forming a triangle with 心 and 悲. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: Loving-Kindness, and Maitreya as 慈氏
satellites.evidence: Maitrī, “friendliness, loving-kindness”, derives from mitra, “friend”, and 慈 renders it. Maitreya, the bodhisattva expected as the next Buddha, appears in Chinese both as 彌勒, a sound loan, and as 慈氏, a translation: “the one of kindness”.

satellites.title: The First Treasure
satellites.evidence: Daodejing ch. 67: 我有三寶，持而保之：一曰慈，二曰儉，三曰不敢為天下先。慈故能勇 — “I have three treasures that I hold and keep: the first is kindness… Being kind, one can be brave.” 慈 was a Daoist virtue long before it was a Buddhist translation.
